rationale: The literature does not provide quantitative evidence that broad forehead (HP:0000337) and high-arched eyebrows (HP:0002553) reach a cumulative penetrance exceeding 75% in molecularly confirmed PSMD12 variant cohorts, nor that they represent the most sensitive craniofacial screening signs. While broad forehead or high forehead is repeatedly observed among craniofacial descriptions in individual case series, eyebrow findings are inconsistently characterized (e.g., described as lateral flaring rather than high-arched eyebrows), and large expansion cohorts emphasize that clinical expressivity of craniofacial anomalies in Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome is marked by high variable expressivity rather than a single invariant upper craniofacial presentation.

evidence.text: In a cohort study expanding the clinical and molecular spectrum of Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (STISS) with 24 additional unrelated patients, the expressivity of most clinical features in STISS was documented to be highly variable, with various dysmorphic facial features noted rather than an invariant high-penetrance upper-craniofacial sign.

source.quote: The expressivity of most clinical features in STISS is highly variable. In addition to previously reported DD/ID, speech delay, cardiac and renal anomalies, we also confirmed preaxial hand abnormalities as a feature of this syndrome.

evidence.text: In the initial cohort defining de novo PSMD12 disruption, specific eyebrow dysmorphisms were noted as lateral flaring of eyebrows rather than high-arched eyebrows.

evidence.text: In six patients from two families with inherited truncating PSMD12 variants, craniofacial findings included broad forehead and frontal bossing with complete penetrance for general neurodevelopmental and craniofacial involvement, but marked inter- and intrafamilial variability.

evidence.text: The Genetic Testing Registry indexes broad forehead as an head and neck abnormality associated with Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome, supporting its presence as a recognized sign without verifying a cumulative penetrance >75%.

conflicts: The hypothesis posits high-arched eyebrows as a core >75% sensitive sign, but original molecular descriptions specifically note lateral flaring of eyebrows, and eyebrow shape is not uniformly reported across series.

Comprehensive expansion cohorts characterize STISS craniofacial features as displaying significant variable expressivity rather than an invariant upper-craniofacial screening constellation sufficient for diagnostic exclusion.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic frequency of standardized upper craniofacial HPO terms across all published PSMD12 cohorts when re-evaluated using objective facial photogrammetry or 3D morphometrics?
new_directions.rationale: Subjective dysmorphic evaluations lead to discordant terms (e.g., broad vs. tall forehead, arched vs. laterally flared eyebrows); computational phenotyping would provide verifiable penetrance statistics.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-craniofacial manifestations, such as preaxial limb defects and type I interferon-stimulated gene signatures, demonstrate higher discriminatory diagnostic sensitivity than facial dysmorphisms in distinguishing STISS from overlapping neurodevelopmental disorders?
new_directions.rationale: Clinical expressivity of craniofacial signs is variable, whereas biochemical biomarkers (interferon signatures) and distinctive limb/renal anomalies may provide higher diagnostic specificity.
